title: The Apostle's "Peace and Greeting" as the Letter Between Summons and Hearing
reading:
When the Apostle opens with peace and greeting, what stands behind that salutation is the whole structural conversation between the Lord and the soul — the summons going forth and the hearing rising up to meet it. The Call that is sent out from the Lord's operative power, and the Hearing by which the rational receives that Call, together compose what may rightly be called a letter: a letter of peace and greeting written from one to another, brother to brother, in which everything that has come to pass between the soul and its source is set down, and everything still to come is set down with it.

The rational, as it is being formed in the natural, receives such a letter. Upon it are inscribed all the tidings of the soul — every state through which it has passed, every contest the proprium has waged against its formation, every answer the forming rational has made when pressed, and every step still prepared to be added to it. Nothing of the soul's history is lost; the whole exchange is held in this correspondence between what is summoned and what hears.

When the rational, fully formed, ascends to the height, the letter ascends with it: the record of its molding, of the strifes that came upon it, of its returning, of the answer it gave amid everything that happened. The Lord's operative power knows every war, every danger, every contest that the proprium and its particular self-loving arrangements raised against the rational while it was being shaped. None of this is hidden from him; he has carried it through with the soul and has its full account.

And the Lord ordering the rational, the truth that comes forth from the Anointed to awaken discrimination within — this too is part of the letter, the further word by which the soul comes to read what has been written and to recognize, in peace, the greeting that has been sent it from the beginning.
